points.description: Role of learning rate: it controls the step size / speed of convergence. Low rate gives slow (overdamped) convergence; higher rate gives faster convergence, possibly oscillating/zigzagging (underdamped) path. Stating only that it controls speed/step size earns part marks.

levels.says: States only that the learning rate controls step size or speed of convergence, without describing the effect of low or high values.

points.description: Danger: if the learning rate is too large (exceeds a critical value) the learning becomes unstable / diverges / overshoots the minimum instead of converging. Merely saying 'too high is bad' or 'zigzags' without instability/divergence earns no more than half.

levels.says: Says a large rate causes oscillation, zigzagging or overshooting but does not state instability/divergence beyond a critical value.

rubric.notes: Full marks: learning rate sets step size/speed of convergence (slow when small, zigzag when large) and a too-large rate beyond a critical value causes instability/divergence. Part marks for partial statements as described. No marks for unrelated answers, e.g. claiming a small rate is dangerous because it diverges.
